UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
/
[PROPOSED| ORDER B — ESTABLISHING MATERIAL FACTS UNDER FEDERAL
RULE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE 56(g)
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Renewed Rule 56 Motion for Partial Summary
Judgment (the "Motion"). The Motion concerns the two letters dated April 22, 2026, signed by
Defendant Katie Hall on the letterhead of Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited
Children ("NCMEC"), that appear in the record at ECF No. 7-5 at 2-3 (the "Letters"). The Court
has considered the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, the parties' submissions, if any, and the
record.
The Court has applied the standard of Rule 56(a) to the agency-and-scope component
identified in Part I of the Motion. The Court does not grant the Motion's request for partial
summary judgment under Rule 56(a) in the form requested, for the reasons stated by the Court on
the record. Because the Court does not grant all the relief requested by the Motion, the Court has
1

considered under Rule 56(g) each material fact listed in Part III of the Memorandum in Support,
the parties' statements of genuine issues, if any, and the opportunity of each affected party to
oppose establishment of each fact. The Court finds that the facts stated below are not genuinely in
dispute. Accordingly, it is hereby
ORDERED that the following facts are established in this action and shall be treated as
established in all further proceedings. Each numbered provision is severable. The Court's omission
of any proposed fact from this Order does not establish any contrary proposition and leaves that
matter for later proceedings.
A.
Hall's employment and the Letters
Katie Hall was an employee of NCMEC and served as NCMEC's Corporate
Counsel when she signed and issued the Letters.
Hall signed each of the two Letters. Each Letter is on NCMEC letterhead. The
signature block of each Letter identifies Hall as "Corporate Counsel."
The first sentence of the body of each Letter states: "In response to your subpoena
issued April 9, 2026, the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children ("NCMEC") provides
its written responses as detailed below." The reference line of one Letter identifies the matter as
"Marvelle Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., et al." The reference line of the other identifies the
matter as "Marvelle Ballentine v. Devin S. Anderson, et al."
B.
The April 9, 2026 materials and formal service
On April 9, 2026, Plaintiff transmitted to NCMEC's Legal Department a letter
giving advance notice of intended subpoenas in two separate matters, together with two signed
subpoena forms and a Schedule A for each. The letter stated that each notice was accompanied by
a signed copy of the draft subpoena "that will be formally served after the notice period has run."
NCMEC received the materials.
2

No subpoena had been formally served on NCMEC when NCMEC issued the
Letters.
Schedule A to each subpoena form directed production of a document sufficient
to show whether NCMEC received or maintains any CyberTipline report, referral, or submission
concerning three identifiers. Schedule A listed the identifiers as "(1) Marvelle J. Ballentine," "(2)
Jay Ballentine," and "(3) the account-level identifier jaychizza@icloud.com," and joined them
with "and/or."
7.
Each Letter
states that NCMEC has received two CyberTipline reports
"concerning (1) Marvelle J. Ballentine, (2) Jay Ballentine, and/or (3) the account-level identifier
jaychizza@icloud.com." The three identifiers and the connector "and/or" in that sentence are the
identifiers and connector that appear in Schedule A.
C.
Plaintiff's account-name history
Before April 22, 2026, Plaintiff did not use the name "Marvelle J. Ballentine" to
create, register, identify, maintain, access, or operate any account on any product or service owned
or operated by Meta Platforms, Inc. that Plaintiff used.
Before April 22, 2026, Plaintiff did not use "Marvelle J. Ballentine" as a
username, profile name, display name, account name, or other identity by which he identified
himself on Facebook, Instagram, Threads, WhatsApp, Oculus, Meta Quest, or any other Meta
product or service that he used.
10.
Before April 22, 2026, Plaintiff did not provide "Marvelle J. Ballentine" to Meta
Platforms, Inc. as the name identifying him for purposes of any Meta account that he created,
maintained, or operated, or as the name identifying any such account. This provision concerns the
identification of accounts. It does not concern litigation filings or other communications.
3

11.
Plaintiff operated the Facebook account that was the subject of Meta Platforms,
Inc.'s July 4, 2022 enforcement action under the name "Jay Ballentine."
12.
Plaintiff included "Marvelle J. Ballentine" in the April 9, 2026 correspondence
and subpoena materials that he transmitted to NCMEC because it is his legal name and the name
under which the underlying federal litigation was pending, and not because he had used that name
to identify or operate any Meta account.
D.
13.
What the Letters do not identify
Neither Letter identifies the electronic service provider or other source that
submitted either report.
14.
Neither Letter supplies a report number for either report.
15.
Neither Letter supplies a report-specific date for either report. Each Letter refers
only to a period "between July 1, 2022 and the present."
16.
Neither Letter states which of the three listed identifiers matched either report.
17.
Neither Letter identifies any particular Facebook account as the subject of either
report.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that, under Rule 56(g), the following fact is established in this
action: Hall signed and issued the Letters on NCMEC's behalf, as NCMEC's agent, within the
course and scope of her employment, in the execution of the service for which NCMEC employed
her. This determination concerns the agency-and-scope component of NCMEC's potential
vicarious liability under Counts I, II, III, and VI of the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5 11
21,195, 216, 230, 258) and nothing else.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that a statement of NCMEC or Hall considered by the Court
in establishing any fact above is not thereby deemed an admission of Meta Platforms, Inc. All
questions of liability against Meta Platforms, Inc. are reserved.
4

It is FURTHER ORDERED that, if leave to file a Second Amended Complaint has been
granted, any agency-and-scope determination stated above applies to the corresponding claims
under the resulting operative pleading.
It is FURTHER ORDERED that this Order does not determine: whether Hall's conduct
was tortious; any defense asserted or available to any Defendant, including the litigation privilege
and any immunity under 18 U.S.C. § 2258D or 34 U.S.C. § 20505; NCMEC's direct liability for
its own conduct; the existence, contents, source, or accuracy of any CyberTipline report; the truth
or falsity of any statement in the Letters as applied to Plaintiff personally; the existence of any
agreement among Defendants; any Defendant's motive or state of mind; any claim against the Doe
Defendants; or any question of damages or other remedy. All such matters are reserved. This Order
is not a final judgment and does not direct the entry of judgment under Rule 54(b).
IT IS SO ORDERED. The Clerk is directed to provide a copy of this Order to Plaintiff at
his address of record and to counsel of record.
Alexandria, Virginia
_ 2026
Rossie D. Alston, Jr.
United States District Judge
